views.title: Around the World in Eighty Days

places.name: London
places.note: The capital, where Phileas Fogg lives by the clock between his house and his club.

places.name: Saville Row
places.note: The Mayfair street of tailors where Fogg lives at No. 7 (Burlington Gardens is round the corner).

places.name: Burlington Gardens
places.note: A short Mayfair street off Savile Row, near Fogg's house.

places.name: Reform Club
places.note: The gentlemen's club on Pall Mall where Fogg dines, reads the papers and plays whist.

places.name: Pall Mall
places.note: The St James's street of grand clubs, the Reform among them.

places.name: Bank of England
places.note: The great bank on Threadneedle Street in the City of London.

places.name: Charing Cross
places.note: The railway station off the Strand where trains leave for Dover and the Continent.

places.name: Dover
places.note: The Kent port facing France across the narrowest part of the Channel.

places.name: Calais
places.note: The French port across the Strait of Dover.

places.name: Paris
places.note: The French capital, the first great city on the road to the East.

places.name: Mont Cenis
places.note: The Alpine pass (and railway tunnel nearby) from France into Italy.

places.name: Turin
places.note: The Piedmontese city on the line from the Alps down to Italy.

places.name: Brindisi
places.note: The port at the heel of Italy where the mail steamers leave for Egypt.

places.name: Egypt
places.note: The land of the Nile, crossed by the new canal from the Mediterranean to the Red Sea.

places.name: Port Said
places.note: The new town at the Mediterranean end of the Suez Canal.

places.name: Suez Canal
places.note: The canal through the desert from the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, opened in 1869.

places.name: Suez
places.note: The town at the Red Sea end of the canal, where the steamers for India call.

places.name: Red Sea
places.note: The long narrow sea between Africa and Arabia, from Suez down to the straits.

places.name: Mocha
places.note: The old coffee port on the Arabian shore of the Red Sea.

places.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
places.note: The strait at the foot of the Red Sea, the 'Gate of Tears', between Arabia and Africa.

places.name: Aden
places.note: The British coaling port at the tip of Arabia, below its volcanic hills.

places.name: Steamer Point
places.note: Aden's harbour quarter (Tawahi), where the steamers coal.

places.name: Indian Ocean
places.note: The ocean between Arabia and India that the mail steamers cross to Bombay.

places.name: India
places.note: British India, crossed by rail from Bombay on the west coast to Calcutta on the east.

places.name: Bombay
places.note: The great port of western India, now Mumbai, where the line across India begins.

places.name: Malabar Hill
places.note: A wooded hill above the sea in Bombay, with temples and fine houses.

places.name: Elephanta
places.note: An island in Bombay harbour famous for its rock-cut cave temples.

places.name: Western Ghauts
places.note: The steep range behind the coast that the railway climbs on leaving Bombay.

places.name: Kandallah
places.note: Khandala, a hill station at the top of the Ghats on the Bombay line.

places.name: Nassik
places.note: Nashik, a holy town on the Godavari river, on the line north-east from Bombay.

places.name: Burhampoor
places.note: Burhanpur, an old Mughal town on the Tapti river.

places.name: Aurungabad
places.note: Aurangabad, Aurangzeb's city in the Deccan, near the Ellora caves.

places.name: Ellora
places.note: The great rock-cut temples near Aurangabad.

places.name: Sutpour Mountains
places.note: The Satpura range in central India, between the Tapti and Narmada valleys.

places.name: Bundelcund
places.note: Bundelkhand, a hilly region of central India, then still half wild.

places.name: Rothal
places.note: A station on the Great Indian Peninsula line between Bombay and Allahabad. Not identified; placed on the route.

places.name: Kholby
places.note: A hamlet in the forest beyond the end of the railway. Invented; placed on the way to Allahabad.

places.name: Pillaji
places.note: A pagoda in the forest of Bundelkhand. Invented; placed between Kholby and Allahabad.

places.name: Allahabad
places.note: The holy city (now Prayagraj) where the Ganges and the Jumna meet, on the line to Calcutta.

places.name: Ganges
places.note: India's sacred river, which the line to Calcutta follows down to Bengal.

places.name: Benares
places.note: Varanasi, the holiest city of the Hindus, on the Ganges.

places.name: Patna
places.note: A large city on the Ganges in Bihar, on the line to Calcutta.

places.name: Bengal
places.note: The province of the lower Ganges, with Calcutta as its capital.

places.name: Burdwan
places.note: Bardhaman, a Bengal town on the line to Calcutta.

places.name: Chandernagor
places.note: Chandannagar, the French trading town on the Hooghly above Calcutta.

places.name: Calcutta
places.note: The capital of British India (now Kolkata), on the Hooghly; the end of the line across India.

places.name: Bay of Bengal
places.note: The great bay east of India, crossed by the steamers from Calcutta to the east.

places.name: Andaman Islands
places.note: A chain of forested islands in the Bay of Bengal.

places.name: Sumatra
places.note: The great island across the Strait of Malacca from the Malay peninsula.

places.name: Straits of Malacca
places.note: The long strait between Sumatra and the Malay peninsula, the gate to the China seas.

places.name: Singapore
places.note: The island port at the tip of the Malay peninsula where the China steamers coal.

places.name: China
places.note: The Chinese Empire, reached through the treaty ports on its coast.

places.name: Macao
places.note: The Portuguese port across the Pearl River estuary from Hong Kong.

places.name: Hong Kong
places.note: The British island colony off south China; its town and harbour are called Victoria.

places.name: Formosa
places.note: Taiwan, the large island off the coast of China.

places.name: Shanghai
places.note: The busy treaty port near the mouth of the Yangtze.

places.name: Nagasaki
places.note: The Japanese port at the southern end of the islands, long the only door to the West.

places.name: Japan
places.note: The island empire, only lately opened to foreigners.

places.name: Yokohama
places.note: The treaty port near Edo (Tokyo) where the Pacific steamers call.

places.name: Pacific
places.note: The great ocean between Japan and California.

places.name: San Francisco
places.note: The Californian port at the western end of the new railway across America.

places.name: Oakland
places.note: The town across the bay from San Francisco where the overland railway begins.

places.name: Sacramento
places.note: California's capital, on the line up into the Sierra Nevada.

places.name: Sierra Nevada
places.note: The snowy range on California's eastern side, crossed by the Pacific Railroad.

places.name: Reno
places.note: A Nevada railway town on the Truckee river.

places.name: Nevada
places.note: The desert state of Nevada, crossed by the railroad east of the Sierra.

places.name: Humboldt River
places.note: The Nevada river and ranges the railway follows across the desert.

places.name: Elko
places.note: A Nevada railway town on the Humboldt river.

places.name: Utah
places.note: The Mormon territory around the Great Salt Lake.

places.name: Great Salt Lake
places.note: The vast salt lake of Utah, with the Mormon city near its shore.

places.name: Salt Lake City
places.note: The Mormon capital, a short branch line from the railroad at Ogden.

places.name: Ogden
places.note: The Utah junction town where the Central Pacific meets the Union Pacific.

places.name: Wahsatch
places.note: The Wasatch range east of the Great Salt Lake.

places.name: Fort Bridger
places.note: An old trading post in south-west Wyoming, on the railroad.

places.name: Green River
places.note: Where the railroad crosses the Green River in Wyoming.

places.name: Bitter Creek
places.note: A creek in the high Wyoming desert, followed by the railroad.

places.name: Bridger Pass
places.note: A pass on the Continental Divide in Wyoming.

places.name: Wyoming
places.note: Wyoming territory, high plains and mountains on the Union Pacific line.

places.name: Fort Halleck
places.note: An old army post below Elk Mountain in Wyoming.

places.name: Medicine Bow
places.note: A Wyoming railway station near the Medicine Bow river and mountains.

places.name: Laramie
places.note: A Wyoming railroad town on the Laramie plains.

places.name: Fort Saunders
places.note: An army post beside Laramie that guarded the railroad builders.

places.name: Rocky Mountains
places.note: The great range of the American West, crossed by the railroad near Laramie.

places.name: Denver
places.note: The Colorado city at the foot of the Rockies, on a branch from the main line.

places.name: Nebraska
places.note: The prairie state crossed by the Union Pacific along the Platte.

places.name: Fort Kearney
places.note: An army post (Fort Kearny) on the Platte river in Nebraska.

places.name: Plum Creek
places.note: A Nebraska station on the Platte (now Lexington).

places.name: Omaha
places.note: The Nebraska city on the Missouri where the Union Pacific begins.

places.name: Missouri
places.note: The great river (and the state) of the American heartland, crossed at Omaha.

places.name: Council Bluffs
places.note: The Iowa town across the Missouri from Omaha.

places.name: Iowa
places.note: The farm state between the Missouri and the Mississippi.

places.name: Mississippi
places.note: The great river of America, crossed by the railway at Davenport.

places.name: Illinois
places.note: The prairie state with Chicago on Lake Michigan.

places.name: Chicago
places.note: The booming city on Lake Michigan, where the eastern railroads meet the western.

places.name: Lake Michigan
places.note: The great lake with Chicago on its southern shore.

places.name: Indiana
places.note: The state east of Illinois.

places.name: Fort Wayne
places.note: An Indiana railway town on the line from Chicago to the east.

places.name: Ohio
places.note: The state between Indiana and Pennsylvania.

places.name: Pittsburgh
places.note: The smoky iron city where the Allegheny and Monongahela make the Ohio.

places.name: Pennsylvania
places.note: The Keystone State, crossed on the way to New York.

places.name: Jersey City
places.note: The railway terminus across the Hudson from New York.

places.name: Hudson
places.note: The river between New Jersey and Manhattan.

places.name: New York
places.note: America's great Atlantic port, where the liners leave for Europe.

places.name: Atlantic
places.note: The ocean between New York and Ireland.

places.name: Newfoundland
places.note: The large foggy island off the North American coast, near the liners' route.

places.name: Bordeaux
places.note: The French wine port on the Gironde.

places.name: Queenstown
places.note: The Irish port (now Cobh) in Cork harbour where Atlantic liners call.

places.name: Dublin
places.note: Ireland's capital, with mail boats across the Irish Sea to England.

places.name: Liverpool
places.note: The great English port on the Mersey, a few hours by express train from London.

places.name: Europe
places.note: The Continent, crossed in a few days by rail on the way to Italy.

places.name: America
places.note: The United States, crossed coast to coast by the new Pacific Railroad.
